_comment: Single source of truth for simulation defaults. BOTH the Python and JS engines load this exact file, so the two can never drift on parameter values. Every number is traceable to docs/RESEARCH_PARAMETERS.md; the service-time models follow Schultz (DLR), the best field-calibrated boarding model in the literature (>400 recorded flights, 282 A320/737 boarding events, validation deviation <5%).
_bagWeights_comment: OVERHEAD-BIN-BOUND pieces per passenger. A personal item that goes under the seat is NOT a piece: it neither occupies a bin slot nor holds up the aisle. Schultz's calibrated set is {1:0.60, 2:0.30, 3:0.10} = 1.5 pieces/pax, i.e. everybody carries at least one. We keep the mean inside the plausible 1.0-1.5 band but allow a modest zero-bag share, because fares that forbid a cabin bag are now common. This is the single designated free parameter for hitting the absolute calibration target in docs/RESEARCH_PARAMETERS.md 11.1; everything else in the service-time model is pinned to the literature.
_partySizeWeights_comment: ASSUMPTION, not a citation. Constructed from Schultz's 73%-alone (business) / 19%-alone (leisure) split as a mixed-traffic compromise. See RESEARCH_PARAMETERS 6 and 12.2.
_walkSpeed_comment: Schultz uses a DETERMINISTIC 0.80 m/s for every agent. We sample per passenger because the product exposes mean and sd as user controls; set walkSpeedSd = 0 to reduce exactly to his configuration (see the schultz_reference fixture). Deliberate deviation, recorded in RESEARCH_PARAMETERS 12.1.
_eliteForwardBias_comment:
Elite and cardholder status is NOT uniformly distributed down the cabin. Status flyers sit in the forward economy rows -- Delta Comfort+, American Main Cabin Extra, United Economy Plus -- because that is what status buys, and the premium cabins are forward by definition. Basic-economy fares are pushed to whatever is left, which is the rear. Modelling status as uniform-random over the whole cabin makes any status-ordered scheme (priority_5tier above all) look far better than it is, because it hands the early groups a random spatial spread instead of the front-loaded one they actually have. See RESEARCH_AIRLINES 7 #6.

The bias is a linear tilt on the eliteMix weights against row position: at the foremost row the status-tier weights are multiplied by (1 + bias) and the basic-economy weight by (1 - bias); at the rearmost row the two are exchanged; the midpoint is untilted, and the cabin-wide mean mix is therefore unchanged. 0 restores the old uniform behaviour exactly. 1.0 is the strongest linear tilt that stays non-negative -- the rearmost row draws no status at all -- and is the shipped value, because the real distribution is concentrated in roughly the forward quarter of economy and a linear ramp already understates that.
_stow_comment: Weibull(shape 1.7, scale 16.0 s) PER PIECE of luggage: mean 14.3 s, sd 8.6 s, measured field mean 13.9 s (Schultz 2018, Aerospace 5(1):27). Total stow time is the SUM of one independent draw per piece, so the variance grows super-linearly with bag count for free -- no exponent hack needed.
_shuffle_comment: Elementary-movement model. One movement (stand / step out / step back / sit) costs Triangular(1.8, 2.4, 3.0) s, mean 2.4 s. The number of movements depends on WHICH seats block, not merely how many. Note 'none' = 1: every passenger pays ~2.4 s simply to sit down, which is a real and non-trivial part of the total.
_stowPass_comment: PARTIAL BLOCKING. A passenger stowing a bag steps out of the aisle centreline into the seat-row gap: the aisle narrows but does not close, and one follower at a time can edge past at this fraction of their walking speed. A SHUFFLING passenger is different and always blocks completely -- when seated occupants stand up to let a window passenger in they are physically in the aisle and nobody gets through. That asymmetry is the point: it makes seat interference strictly more expensive than bag stowing. Schultz has no partial-blocking term (a cellular model cannot express one), so this is a deliberate deviation. It is what makes absolute boarding times credible; the cost is that strategy advantages compress toward parity. Full evidence and the factor sweep: docs/RESEARCH_PARAMETERS.md 12.3.

_stowPassSpeedFactor_options.label: Strict aisle blocking (Schultz-comparable)
_stowPassSpeedFactor_options.note: A stowing passenger closes the aisle outright, as in Schultz's cellular model. Use this for apples-to-apples comparison against his published figures, and when strategy-ratio magnitudes matter more than absolute times. Costs ~50% on absolute single-door boarding time.

_stowPassSpeedFactor_options.label: Difficult squeeze
_stowPassSpeedFactor_options.note: Edging past somebody wrestling a roller bag in a 19-inch aisle.

_stowPassSpeedFactor_options.label: Normal squeeze (default)
_stowPassSpeedFactor_options.note: Calibrated: puts single-door boarding on Schultz's field regression.

_stowPassSpeedFactor_options.label: Easy sidestep
_stowPassSpeedFactor_options.note: A wide aisle and a considerate stower.

_door_comment: Measured inter-arrival of passengers at the aircraft door, exponential with mean 3.7 s (Schultz). This is a major serialising constraint: on a 186-seat single-door boarding it alone accounts for ~11.5 minutes.
_bin_comment: binBagsPerRowSide lives on the AIRCRAFT (bin volume is an airframe property and varies enormously -- 1 bag/row-side on a legacy E175, 4 on an A320neo with Airspace XL bins). Set it here only to override the airframe. Search/gate-check penalties are extrapolation, not literature: no peer-reviewed source publishes a gate-check time penalty (RESEARCH_PARAMETERS 7, 12.2).
_doorAwareZones_comment: With more than one boarding door enabled, sequence every spatially-ordered strategy WITHIN each door's own region -- far from THAT door first -- instead of across the whole cabin. A cabin-wide rear-first order is far-end-first at 1L and near-end-first at 2L, and near-end-first is the front-to-back pathology; see ENGINE_SPEC 4.1 and the `doorSequencing` metric in ENGINE_SPEC 7. Set false to recover the naive cabin-wide ordering, which is instructive to contrast and is what every published zone scheme actually describes. No effect with a single door.
_nonCompliance_comment: Schultz's measured conformance rate is 85%, so 15% of passengers ignore the group they were called in.
_openSeating_comment: avoid_neighbours is the realistic default: unassigned-seat passengers demonstrably spread out rather than filling from the front. The literal front-filling policies (aisle_first / front_first) are kept because the product exposes them, but they are pathological -- everyone stows at the same advancing frontier, which fully serialises the boarding.
_constants_comment: Physical constants and the PCG32 stream layout (ENGINE_SPEC 1.3). The stream numbers live here, next to everything else both engines load, because a stream index copied into two languages is exactly the kind of constant that drifts. PAX_STREAM and ORDER_STREAM are the two whole-run streams. DOOR_STREAM_BASE + doorIndex is one stream per door, advanced once per release, so the k-th arrival at a door draws the same gap whatever order the queue is in. SERVICE_STREAM_BASE + paxId * SERVICE_STREAM_STRIDE + phase is one stream per passenger per service phase, so a passenger's own draws are invariant to when they board -- that is what makes common random numbers complete. Stream 3 was the old single event-ordered `sim` stream and is retired, not reused.
